content.title: Lakers 107, Rockets 98: Houston's offense struggles without Kevin Durant in Game 1
content.text: LOS ANGELES - The Houston Rockets, without Kevin Durant, fell to the Los Angeles Lakers in their playoff opener, 107-98 on Saturday night.Houston's offense couldn't find a rhythm. The Rockets shot just 37.6% from the field and 33.3% from 3-point range. Alperen Şengün and Amen Thompson combined for 36 points but shot a combined 13-for-37.AdvertisementLeBron James scored just 19 points but had 13 assists, orchestrating a Lakers offense that made 60.6% of its field goals. Luke Kennard led Los Angeles with 27 points, including 5-for-5 from distance."As a shooter, you know when it feels right, so I was just trying to be aggressive and look for my shot whenever I could," Kennard told ABC's Lisa Salters after the win.Game 2 is at 9:30 p.m. Tuesday at Crypto.com Arena. - Varun ShankarLAKERS 107, ROCKETS 98FGFTRebJ.Smith Jr.43:025-143-55-120116Thompson43:077-183-64-77417Sengun35:596-197-94-86519Okogie26:252-42-20-0127Sheppard35:556-200-00-18217Eason23:557-70-13-102416Capela11:201-20-01-2002Holiday10:470-40-00-0020Tate9:301-52-24-4024Totals240:0035-9317-2521-44242298Percentages: FG .376, FT .680.3-Point Goals: 11-33, .333 (Sheppard 5-14, J.Smith Jr. 3-9, Eason 2-2, Okogie 1-2, Tate 0-1, Thompson 0-1, Holiday 0-2, Sengun 0-2).AdvertisementTeam Rebounds: 11. Lakers33172532-107A_19,057 (18,997).Here's how the game played out:LeBron daggerThis one probably already was over, but LeBron James backing down Amen Thompson, then hitting a fadeaway felt like the final nail in the coffin. Lakers lead 98-84 with 2:36 remaining. James has 17 points, 12 assists and 8 rebounds. - Matt YoungLittle Rockets runThe Rockets are on a mini 8-3 run to cut the Lakers' lead to 91-80 with six minutes remaining, which was enough to get Lakers coach JJ Redick to call a timeout after a Tari Eason 3. - Matt YoungAdvertisementLakers opening it upBiggest lead of the night for the Lakers, who are up 88-72 after 3-pointers from LeBron James and Luke Kennard.The Rockets are shooting better from 3-point range (39.1%) than they are from the field (33.8%). The former is a great mark. The latter is disastrous.Alperen Şengün has just 11 points, 10 missed shots on 13 attempts and under eight minutes left to mount a serious comeback. - Varun ShankarDisheartening for RocketsWhat's got to be particularly discouraging about the Rockets being down double digits with eight minutes remaining is that the Lakers are doing this without a heroic effort from LeBron James. The Lakers star has been great, of course, with 11 assists, but he's scored just 13 points. Without Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, you'd think James would have to carry a heavier load than that. - Matt YoungAdvertisementEnd of the third: Rockets trail Lakers, 75-66Amen Thompson missed two free throws to end the quarter. Houston was 2 of 6 from the line in the quarter. The Lakers were 11 of 15. - Reid LaymanceRoyal letdownThe Rockets trailed 66-58 when LeBron exited the game. He re-enters and they're … down 73-63. - Varun ShankarRockets getting T'd upJae'Sean Tate just got called for a loose-ball foul and rose in protest - earning a technical foul as well.And now Ime Udoka gets called for a technical. - Varun ShankarTari Eason finds scoresheetTari Eason averaged 10.5 points per game during the regular season, but it took him until just now for him to get his first shot attempt in this one. He drove past Jaxson Hayes for a bucket that cut the Lakers' lead to 67-60 with 3:30 left in the third. - Matt YoungAdvertisementRockets change it upRockets in what looks like a 2-3 zone. - Varun ShankarOdd move by LeBronUnusual play there. As Lakers were off and running, LeBron James appeared to seek out contact with Jabari Smith Jr., as they headed down the court. Smith grabbed James and was whistled for a foul. Obviously the right call for Smith grabbing the Lakers star, but unusual for James to make contact like that. Lakers have stretched lead to 65-56 with 5 minutes left in the third quarter. It was called a transition take foul, giving the Lakers a free throw and the ball - Matt YoungHi, FredLeBron James just came over and dapped up Fred VanVleet after the timeout. The two chatted for a moment. - Varun ShankarAdvertisementA big missMassive swing against the Rockets. Josh Okogie misses an alley-oop layup on a 3-on-1 fastbreak and the Lakers come back with a Rui Hachimura 3-pointer. - Varun ShankarLong distanceReed Sheppard opened the half with a 3 to give the Rockets their first lead since it was 4-2. Rockets lead 51-50 just a minute into the second half. - Matt YoungChuck not impressedOn the ABC halftime show, Charles Barkley didn't have kind words for the Rockets offense in that first half. "The Lakers are playing smart, efficient. The Rockets, I have no idea what they're doing," Barkley said. "They're just like, the first person that gets it, just jack it up. They've got nothing happening out there." - Matt YoungAdvertisementHalftime: Lakers 50, Rockets 48Houston shot 20% from the field in the second quarter but still won it by two points - the product of going 10-for-11 on free throws. Şengün made all four of his foul shots. He leads Houston with 11 points at halftime.Deandre Ayton has 12 for the Lakers. LeBron James has six points and 10 assists. The Lakers are at 64.7% from the field - some of that is hot shooting, but Houston's defense needs more physicality. It seemed like the Rockets turned things up late in the second quarter. The Lakers didn't score for the last 1:52 of the half and Houston forced four turnovers in that stretch to cut an eight-point deficit to two at the break. - Varun ShankarFrustration for Amen ThompsonAmen Thompson has been quite frustrated with his lack of whistles drawn so far tonight - including on that last block (which looked clean on replay).AdvertisementThompson has attacked downhill repeatedly and is 2-for-7. He has has taken two free throws and made both.Thompson was right to be frustrated on that last floater. He got clobbered. - Varun ShankarAmen Thompson stays inAmen Thompson stays in the game and makes both of his free throws. It's 44-38 Lakers with 6:22 left in the first half. - Varun ShankarAmen Thompson shaken upAmen Thompson is limping a bit as he comes to the Rockets' bench. He landed hard after going up for a layup against Jarred Vanderbilt. - Varun ShankarLakers take biggest leadA nine-point lead (40-31) marks the Lakers' biggest advantage of the game. - Greg RajanAdvertisementJarred Vanderbilt sightingJarred Vanderbilt wasn't expected to be much of a factor in this series for the Lakers, but the Houston native already has knocked down a 3-pointer. Vanderbilt, in his eighth season in the NBA, hit a corner 3 that put the Lakers up 38-31 early in the second quarter. The 27-year-old, who went to Victory Prep Academy in Houston, shot 29% from 3 this season. - Matt YoungThrough 12 minutesEnd of the first: Rockets trail the Lakers, 33-29.LeBron James has four points and eight assists. Luke Kennard is leading Los Angeles - which shot 78.9% in the frame - with 11 points. Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Şengün have 15 combined points on 6-for-10 shooting for the Rockets. - Varun ShankarAdvertisementEnd first quarter: Lakers 33, Rockets 29The Rockets are mostly holding their own, but the Lakers are shooting a sizzling 78.9% to hold a four-point lead after the opening 12 minutes. - Greg RajanFinally, Jae'Sean Tate sees playoff actionEntering the game and making his playoff debut: Jae'Sean Tate.The Rockets made the playoffs the year before Tate joined the team and missed the postseason for his first four seasons. They made it last year, but he did not play due to injury. - Varun ShankarLeBron the facilitatorWhile he has four points, LeBron James also has seven eight assists in the game's first eight minutes. Per the Associated Press, that's his career playoff high for assists in the opening quarter. - Greg RajanAdvertisementLakers 17, Rockets 14Lakers take the first timeout of the series. Rockets with five straight points to get within 17-14 with 6:11 left in the first quarter.LeBron has four points and four assists already, making both of his shots. He's still a force. - Varun ShankarTough shooting startThe Rockets are 2-of-6 from the field to the Lakers' 6-of-7 through four-plus minutes. - Greg RajanSheppard strategiesYou're seeing the Lakers try and get Reed Sheppard switched onto LeBron James often in the early going by having Sheppard's man, Marcus Smart, set a screen for James.AdvertisementThe Rockets are working to avoid it by having Sheppard aggressively come up on James before retreating to Smart, giving James' original defender time to recover. - Varun ShankarAuspicious startJosh Okogie starts with the LeBron assignment. He blows up a screen, gets a steal and gets fouled. Nice start for Houston. - Varun ShankarTonight's startersHere is tonight's Rockets starting lineup:Reed SheppardJosh OkogieAmen ThompsonJabari Smith Jr.Alperen ŞengünAnd here are the Lakers' starters:Marcus SmartLuke KennardLeBron JamesRui HachimuraDeandre Ayton- Varun ShankarThe Rockets will not have Kevin Durant for Saturday's playoff opener against the Los Angeles Lakers, coach Ime Udoka said.AdvertisementDurant was questionable entering the game with a right knee contusion.He had a healthy but arduous regular season, playing 78 games and finishing second among all players in minutes played. - Varun ShankarHow to watchWhen: 7:30 p.m. SaturdayWhere: Crypto.com Arena, Los AngelesTV: ABC with Mike Breen (play-by-play), Richard Jefferson and Tim Legler (analysts) and Lisa Salters (sideline reporter).Radio: 790 AMRecommended readingThis article originally published at Lakers 107, Rockets 98: Houston's offense struggles without Kevin Durant in Game 1.
